findings.different: An OS condition on a single CPU-only test whose subject builds on every platform, not a parent module condition or a GPU admission.

findings.name: Un-gated Metal draw tests need an Apple-only dev-dependency
findings.different: Not a hidden test, a missing admission or an OS condition: un-gating thrum-asset-gpu's draw test module left it using serde_json, which Cargo.toml declares only for macOS and iOS, so the crate's lib tests no longer compile on Linux or Windows.

findings.name: Water scene tests do not compile off macOS
findings.different: Not a hidden test, a missing admission or an OS condition: the water example's 11 GPU test targets import thrum-app APIs that exist only on macOS, so they fail to compile on Linux and Windows.

briefs.task:
Plan two pieces of work from the owner's requests of 14 Nov 2026. The owner then said: "can you not just plan and drive that work?" So the decisions below are made; plan them as buildable milestones, not human decisions.

1) Code review fixes. A whole-repository review is at /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum/tmp/code-review-2026-11-14/CODE-REVIEW.md, with slices in sections/ beside it. Copy it into docs/evidence/code-review-2026-11-14/ and plan its fixes. The canonical shapes are already written in .agents/skills/thrum-engineering/references/patterns.md (review step 1); add the review's mechanical repo_check rules. Then follow its order of attack: confirmed bugs first (H01, H09, M41, H11, H14), then typed Rust-WGSL records and typed pass keys (T1, T2), test support and one GPU gate (T6), one device recipe and host core (T4), error convention (T3), performance (T12), and renames and splits (T9, T10) as one planned architecture milestone, then hygiene (T13). Give each fix to the module that owns the code, or a new module where none does. Modules are cut by isolation and ownership, and each delivers milestone by milestone in order; do not split CLOUDS or WATERS or change their milestones. Sequence work so it does not rewrite files that running builders hold (CULLING M3, APPLE-PRESENTATION M3, APPLE-TILE M10, CREATOR M3, EFFECT-GRAPH M3, ATMOSPHERE M9, CLOUDS M1, WATERS M1); later milestones of those modules may be rebased onto it.
   H03 decision: no Git history rewrite (it would need a force-push to main under many live worktrees). Plan the forward fix only: bulk media and archives leave the tracked tree under docs/ASSET-LIFECYCLE.md's storage rules (untrack at HEAD, keep selected small evidence), and repo_check stops new bulk binaries being committed. Keep evidence links that reviews depend on resolvable.

2) Separate the game from the engine. Owner: "it sounds like we're blurring the lines between the engine and the game a ton. Please let's separate out the game as much as we can, it shouldn't even sit in the same code base ideally." Today examples/v1-game (26k lines) holds engine host and shell code (host, window, browser, camera, projection, controls), engine qualification rigs (H20), and engine tests compile its source (H02/H13); thrum-cook depends on examples/asset-loop (H19); ARCHITECTURE places CLOUDS and PUDDLES selections in v1-game. Design the end state where the game lives in its own repository and depends only on the engine's public API: engine host/shell code moves into engine crates (also H15/M03), qualification moves into the owning crates or an engine-side harness, shared fixtures move to engine test support, and repo_check enforces the boundary. Stage it: first make the boundary real inside this repository, then move the game out.
   Repository decision: the game moves to a new local Git repository at /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum-games (v1-game now; the swarm game later), with no remote until the owner asks for one. It consumes the engine through Cargo path dependencies on a sibling Thrum checkout, so engine changes surface in the game at once; switching to pinned git revisions is a later step once the engine has releases. The last stage creates that repository, moves the game with its history-free copy, and leaves Thrum with no game code. The upcoming swarm game follows the same shape from the start. V1 still exits through the showcase game, so keep its milestones buildable throughout and say how the V1 gate is verified once the game lives outside.

Say which new milestones can start at once, and which wait for running builders.

Fix every Must Fix so the designs pass, resolving the GAME-SPLIT/TEST-SUPPORT interface conflicts together (one authority for each shared fixture). Move Thrum onto the proof regime the owner approved, using orchestrate 2.3.1, in one pass, tonight.

Why: delivery stalled under proofs. In the last 24h, 4 milestones reached Ready for Review against 419 commits, and 163 of 288 background jobs failed. The single GPU lock was 92-94% busy, mostly with rebase, re-prove and merge attempts that failed. The design is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ryannel-Workspace-thrum/e5ff9d25-dfb5-4b37-a169-158dbdac268c/scratchpad/proof-regime.md; section 4 has the steps T1a-T9. The script now does much of what it proposed: shared resources, lock hold limits, `reads`, a merge queue and main-branch checks with retry and bisect. Read ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ryannel-skills/orchestrate/2.3.1/skills/orchestration/build/SKILL.md, build-milestone/SKILL.md and plan-module/references/proofs.md before you change anything.

The owner's words, to quote wherever a change is the human's decision: "Ok, let's get the script and skill changes done then once we've got orchestrate to where it needs to be, let's get the lead on Thrum working." and "We want all these fixes in place before I head to bed tonight." The owner also confirmed "Go ahead" in the lead session on 15 Nov. That covered: a warning-only gate, an hourly verifier on main, `gpu: 2, chrome: 1`, BASELINE-GUARD re-planned, the rule and skill text updated, and accepting that an unintended image change can sit on main for about 2 hours.

Carry out, adjusted for 2.3.0:
- **T1a.** The exact-baselines gate in `./dev check` warns instead of refusing. Declare the verifier as a `Main-branch check` in ORCHESTRATE.md (every 1h; lock gpu; a timeout that fits the ~16 min run). Record a dated ruling in ARCHITECTURE.md's Exact baselines.
- **T1b.** The script now does the sentinel's shared run, retry, bisect and naming the culprit. Re-plan BASELINE-GUARD down to what remains Thrum's own (for example the verify command and the CPU ownership guard), and decide what happens to its in-flight M2 on branch build/baseline-guard.
- **Verifier items.** Open milestones carry about 116 items whose check runs `exact_baselines.py verify`. Changing `check` text resets progress, which `lock` and `reads` don't. Weigh repointing them at `python3 "$ORCHESTRATE_SCRIPT" main-check <name>` (no lock of its own) against having the verifier read the shared result. Pick the option that disturbs open branches least, and say why.
- **T2-T5,** as the report says. In T4, never nest gpu inside merge, and never hold a lock while waiting for a person.
- **T6.** Declare `Shared resources: gpu: 2, chrome: 1`; that capacity change is what ends most of the queueing. Give each item the lock its device needs for capacity. Use `gpu.alone` only for a run that needs the whole GPU, such as all its memory. It does not make timings trustworthy, because builders compiling elsewhere take no lock.
- **T9's timing policy is the timing fix.** Within a milestone, a timing item becomes a loose benchmark tripwire that catches a collapse. Precise numbers move to the module's last milestone, measured in one sitting with builders paused. Sweep the timing items to that line.
- **Fold T7-T8 in** where they're cheap; otherwise record them as later work.

Constraints:
- Don't edit the orchestrate skills or agent_loop.py. If the script blocks a step, stop that step and write down what happened.
- Keep open branches mergeable.
- Work in the lead worktree or your own; never touch the main checkout's tmp/.

Done when:
- the changes are merged to main, `./dev check-docs` passes and the plan checks pass;
- an open branch can merge without a fresh exact-image proof;
- the main-branch check is declared and `main-check --due` lists it;
- your report names the commits, every module whose design review is now owed, and anything you held back because it goes beyond what the owner approved.

Plan the cleanup that the 20 November review found. The owner's request that day was: "We want to do a code cleanup and consolidation for Thrum." The purpose is to make Thrum cheaper to change: a shorter merge gate, no tools, records or code that nothing uses, and no proof heavier than the fault it guards. It must not change what the engine draws, simulates or sends.

Start from /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum/tmp/cleanup-2026-11-20/REPORT.md. Read it in place; don't copy it or edit it. Beside it, results.json holds every finding, findings/<reviewer>.md holds the full write-ups, and verified/<reviewer>-<n>.md holds the second agents' corrections. Where a verifier corrected a finding, the verifier is right.

In scope: the report's sections 1 to 4 (gate time, dead tools and records, dead engine code, and small API changes that delete stubs). Also in scope: the parts of section 6 that are code or files, meaning the fixtures and record writers that still use docs/evidence, and the water settings that are parsed twice. Section 5, the test kit, belongs to TEST-SUPPORT as a milestone after its M2, so plan it there. Section 7 needs designs of its own: list each part as not planned, with one line each.

Section 6's plan and settings text belongs to the lead and the planners:
- L8-01: no rule says a Done item's check is history, so about 770 path mentions are treated as frozen.
- L8-05: `! grep` and `test ! -e` checks pass when their path is missing (HOST M4.5, CLOUDS M14.13, SHOWCASE M9.7, HOST M3.2).
- L8-07: ten open items ask for new tracked files under docs/evidence, which the merge guard refuses.
Fix those in the open done-when items and in ORCHESTRATE.md where it's within planner authority. Name any change that only the orchestrate skill can make, and keep that out of this plan.

What the plan must respect:
- A done-when item names a behaviour, not a file location. SHOWCASE M9.6 failed review over a byte-identical fixture move because its items named paths.
- Up to three Claude builders (Opus 5.5 medium) can work at once. Shape the work so that milestones with disjoint files can run side by side, as separate modules if that's what it takes, and say which ones can.
- Other builders are live, on Codex, in APPLE-PRESENTATION, HOST, RAY-TRACING, REVIEW-RENDER, SESSION, TEST-SUPPORT and RENDER-2D. The findings' verifier notes say which files are busy and which open done-when items name them. Declare each milestone's files, so the lead can confirm them before a builder starts.
- A deletion that drops a capability or a proof is the owner's call. Carry each one as an assumption, with the other choice stated. That covers the headless release-trust toolchain (8,500 lines), the nine benches nothing runs, the ten-minute gale soak (actual_gale_keeps_the_fleet_in_contact_on_metal) moving from the gate to a main-branch check with a 60-second run left in the gate, and the reference tests that the 17 November bar may retire. The state-delta codec stays unless SESSION's design changes, because that design says keep.
- scripts/ is a covered path for exact baselines, so script deletions land together.
- Changes to the gate's machinery (the test profile, nextest) are measured before they're switched on.
- Order by payoff. Gate time comes first, because every merge pays it.

Done when the design has passed its review and the plan is merged.

2. Apply the hardening pass at /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum/tmp/cleanup-2026-11-20/HARDENING.md. Read it in place; it was written at 07339e923, so check each point against today's text.
- A1: GATE-TIME M1 merges first in wave 1, after one release-build run of its tests, with the debug-on-main fallback the file describes.

3. The owner's decision of 20 Nov: the merge tier is targeted. Every merge runs only the tests for what the change touches, and the full workspace runs on main. Replace the whole-workspace merge check. The design must say:

Measure the saving before the switch is turned on.

4. Not yet answered by the owner, so carry these as Assumption: lines with the other choice stated: a hard stop when a test binary in the merge tier runs over three minutes, and hourly runs of the feature-gated tests on main.

5. Keep each milestone's files table and the wave table current, because the lead confirms files before each builder starts. Feature builders are held until this programme lands (owner: "Cleanup first"), so ordering can assume a quiet machine once the live Codex milestones finish.

The owner approved a test guardrail set for planning on 21 Nov ("Yes, plan it"). Purpose: the fast-test habits (small worlds, CPU first, few binaries, long runs off the merge path) hold without anyone remembering them. What must hold every time goes in the merge check, because Codex and Claude builders both pass through it; no Claude hooks, since Codex builders never run them. Place the work in GATE-TIME and/or TEST-SUPPORT as milestones with provable items; a planner step just before you placed four related test-speed changes (read its commit and notes first, and build on them rather than duplicating). Don't change any milestone that has started.
Merge-check rules, beside the ratchet rules in scripts/shape_rules.py:
1. A test over the limit is stopped and fails. .config/nextest.toml has it at 60 s (slow at 10 s, stopped after 6 periods); it drops to 10 s once GATE-TIME M9 lands.
2. The tests exempt from that limit (the override filter in .config/nextest.toml, eight today) can only shrink.
3. The main-tier list .config/long-tests.txt (11 entries today) can only shrink unless a plan says otherwise. shape_rules.py never grants an increase over Git history, so state how a plan raises the count (for example the rule's version).
4. The number of test binaries can only go down (265 in GATE-TIME M8's runs). This depends on the fewer-binaries change: freeze the count first, then consolidate.
Not a gate: the check's report already prints step times and slowest tests; add summed test time and GPU-test seconds. A gate on total time would fail good work (load averages of 19 to 23 during checks).
Also settle: the hourly `workspace-tests` main-branch check (`./dev check-all`, ORCHESTRATE.md) takes no `lock gpu` yet runs the 221 GPU tests, so it contends with builders unqueued. Decide whether it takes the lock or its GPU tests move elsewhere, unless the previous step already did.
Engineering skill (.agents/skills/thrum-engineering/SKILL.md): one short block on writing a test that replaces the "Unit tests" and "GPU tests" rows rather than adding to them, with pattern entries the new rules' messages link to: prove a behaviour on the smallest world that shows it; test logic on the CPU and open a device only for what a GPU alone can show, at the test kit's small target; step simulated time, never wait on the clock; add to an existing test binary; a full-size or long run is a main-tier test and needs a plan's say. The owner keeps always-loaded text short: the block stays about that size and AGENTS.md gets nothing. "The test kit's small target" doesn't exist yet; it belongs with TEST-SUPPORT M3 or M4 (not started).
ORCHESTRATE.md "What is proved, and how hard": each done-when item says whether its check is a guard that stays (and so meets the limits) or a record that runs once and whose tools are deleted at close; a plan that adds a GPU test or a main-tier test says what only that test can show; a reviewer reruns the tests a change touches, not the whole check, and questions any new test over about a second. No lint can tell a GPU test should have been a CPU test; that stays with the reviewer line.
The owner accepted the 10 s limit and that a new long test needs a plan decision. Done when the plans, and any ORCHESTRATE.md text that is the planner's to write, are amended and committed with a short note saying where each part went.
